parsed.why: Protective statutes (accommodations, facilities access, nonsurgical markers, shield law) with documented enforcement: court-ordered care resumption, custody consent decree. Still bound by national border-document/entry regime and federal-facility order; youth coverage suspended October 2026.

Governor's order ends state recognition and backs birth-sex spaces; markers need surgery; care ban upheld; custody assault dismissed as de minimis; no state gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute.

Operating protections: public accommodations, gender-identity hate crime, panic-defence repeal, gender-neutral restrooms, enforceable shield law, self-ID markers; documented acceptance (school barred for forfeiting). National entry/document regime still applies.

Birth-sex facility law for schools and government buildings, reporting form and documentary defence no visitor can meet; care, sports, dorm bans; offset partly by gender-identity hate-crime statute, nonsurgical marker route, employment/housing protections.

Broadest facility ban with private right of action; no state gender-identity protection in any category and no state hate-crime law; surgical marker requirement; care and sports bans; rated worst for targeting trans adults.
